correctness.rationale: Let V be an orthonormal basis matrix for the range of P and g_i=Vᵀω_i. Then the g_i are independent standard Gaussians in R^r. For each J the Nyström matrix is λVΠ_JVᵀ, where Π_J projects onto the span of the g_j with j∈J; this follows from G_J(G_JᵀG_J)^†G_Jᵀ=Π_J, including the empty case. Thus f(B_J)=cVΠ_JVᵀ. For k≤r the added direction is the held-out residual, whose squared norm is χ²_d conditional on the other columns. To check the covariance, condition off the other k−2 columns, leaving two independent Gaussian vectors in q=d+1 dimensions. Their residual energies have independent squared radii times the same factor 1−U, where U is the squared directional cosine. Conditional on U the energies are independent and each has mean q(1−U); consequently covariance is q²Var(U)=2(q−1)/(q+2), since E U=1/q and E U²=3/[q(q+2)]. Exchangeability yields Var(H)=[Var(H_i)+(k−1)Cov(H_i,H_j)]/k and E S=[Var(H_i)−Cov(H_i,H_j)]/k. This verifies the risk, the calibration ratio, and the k=r limits at fixed c. At k=1 the marginal law gives the risk and there is no indicator; for k≥r+1 every leave-one-out span fills the active range and both estimator and indicator are exact. The argument is for raw Gaussian probes and does not require c>0. The frozen script was inspected, not executed; its residual checks do not independently verify the pseudoinverse identity.
